summary: Extends HTML to support a wide variety of tables. It was an experimental specification and is now historic, replaced by RFC 2854.

eli5.summary: Before this, web pages had trouble showing neat rows and columns. This described a way to put things in grids on a page. It is now historic.

subtitle: Structured grids for displaying rows and columns of data.

tldr.problem: HTML lacked a standard way to display tabular data. Early tables were created informally, and there was no consensus on syntax, alignment, or how to handle complex structures like merged cells or grouped rows.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 1942 defines TABLE, CAPTION, COL, COLGROUP, THEAD, TFOOT, TBODY, TR, TH, and TD elements with attributes for alignment, spanning, and borders. It includes two layout algorithms (fixed and auto) to handle varying content sizes and provides support for accessibility (axis labels for screen readers) and multiple rendering targets (speech, braille).
tldr.outcome: The table model became the foundation for HTML tables in all subsequent versions. It is now historic, replaced by RFC 2854 and later standards, but tables remain widely used for data display.

facts.label: Core table elements
facts.value: TABLE, TR (row), TH (header cell), TD (data cell)

facts.label: Grouping elements
facts.value: THEAD, TBODY, TFOOT for row groups; COLGROUP, COL for column groups

facts.value: ROWSPAN and COLSPAN for merging cells

today: RFC 1942 is now Historic and was superseded by RFC 2854 (HTML 4.01) and later standards. However, tables as defined here remain a core part of HTML and are still widely used for displaying tabular data, though CSS and more semantic approaches are now preferred for layout.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
HTML Tables provide a way to organize data into rows and columns. A table starts with an optional CAPTION, followed by one or more rows (TR elements), each containing header cells (TH) or data cells (TD). Cells can span multiple rows and columns, and rows can be grouped into head, body, and foot sections (THEAD, TBODY, TFOOT).

The model is designed to be simple for basic tables but extensible for complex ones. It supports features like character-based alignment (aligning numbers on a decimal point), control over borders and rules between cells, and markup for accessibility (such as axis labels for screen readers and braille renderers).
sections.eli5: A table is made of rows and cells, like a spreadsheet. Each cell can say if it is a header or data, and cells can stretch across multiple rows or columns. You can control the borders and how things line up.

sections.title: Design Rationale
sections.content:
The table model draws from the CALS (Computer-Aided Logistics Support) table model used in SGML, word processors, and desktop publishing. A key goal was backwards compatibility with the Netscape browser's table implementation, which was already widely deployed.

The model prioritizes simplicity: simple tables use minimal markup, while more complex ones use additional elements only when needed. It avoids embedding rendering information in markup (preferring style sheets) but allows basic control over borders and spacing for practical use. The design also supports incremental display for large tables and both visual and non-visual rendering (braille, speech).
sections.eli5: The designers wanted tables to be easy to write by hand but also work with spreadsheets and design tools. They borrowed ideas from CALS and made sure it matched what Netscape was already doing.

sections.title: Table Structure and Elements
sections.content:
A TABLE element contains a CAPTION (optional), column definitions (COL or COLGROUP elements), optional THEAD, optional TFOOT, and one or more TBODY sections. Each section contains TR (row) elements, which contain TH or TD elements.

COLGROUP groups columns and allows default alignment and width properties to be set for a set of columns. COL elements define properties for individual columns or column ranges. THEAD, TFOOT, and TBODY allow rows to be grouped, which is useful for repeating headers and footers when printing or scrolling. Cells can have ROWSPAN and COLSPAN attributes to span multiple rows or columns. Cells also support AXIS (a short label) and AXES (a list of relevant axis labels) for accessibility.
sections.eli5: Tables have a head section (headers that repeat), a foot section (like a total row), and body sections. You can group columns and say how wide they should be. Cells can stretch across rows or columns.

sections.title: Alignment and Rendering Attributes
sections.content:
Cells support horizontal alignment (ALIGN: left, center, right, justify, or char for alignment on a specific character like a decimal point), character alignment with CHAR and CHAROFF attributes, and vertical alignment (VALIGN: top, middle, bottom, or baseline).

The TABLE element has BORDER (frame width), FRAME (which sides of the outer frame to draw), and RULES (which internal lines to draw). FRAME values include void, above, below, hsides, lhs, rhs, vsides, box, and border. RULES values include none, groups, rows, cols, and all. CELLPADDING controls space inside cells, and CELLSPACING controls space between cells. Alignment can be inherited from the column, row, or table, with a defined precedence order.
sections.eli5: You can say if text in a cell is left, center, right, or lined up on a decimal point. You control what borders and lines show. Cells inherit alignment from their row or column if not set directly.

sections.title: Layout Algorithms
sections.content:
RFC 1942 defines two layout algorithms. The fixed layout algorithm assumes the number of columns is known (specified with the COLS attribute). Column widths are set according to relative or absolute width specifications, with space allocated to relative-width columns after absolute-width columns.

The autolayout algorithm is used when COLS is not specified. It makes two passes through the table: the first determines the minimum and maximum width of each cell (with line wrapping disabled), and the second assigns column widths to fit the available space. For nested tables, the algorithm recursively applies the same logic. The algorithm handles character alignment, which requires tracking content left and right of the alignment character.
sections.eli5: The fixed algorithm takes the column widths you give it and uses them. The auto algorithm figures out how wide each column needs to be by looking at what is inside, then stretches or shrinks to fit the page.

sections.title: Security and Accessibility
sections.content:
The RFC notes that tables can contain all forms of HTML content, including nested tables, forms, and other elements. Security considerations depend on the content within cells.

For accessibility, the AXIS and AXES attributes allow cells to label themselves for speech rendering. When reading a table aloud, a screen reader can announce the relevant headers for each cell, making tables usable for visually impaired users. The THEAD, TBODY, and TFOOT structure aids text-to-speech conversion and allows rendering to braille.
sections.eli5: Cells can tell screen readers what their headers are, so someone listening to a table understands which row and column each piece of data belongs to.
